skills.name: Writing mechanics: punctuation and clause boundaries

note.text: Punctuation guides interpretation rather than replacing sentence structure. A comma alone normally does not join independent clauses in this edited prose. A full stop, semicolon or suitable conjunction can supply a boundary; this exercise specifies the choice. A possessive apostrophe belongs to the owner expression. Paired quotation marks identify direct speech; list commas separate items. Conventions can allow alternatives, such as a final list comma. Follow the teacher’s required quotation and examination style.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to edit boundaries, possession, a list and direct quotation without changing meaning. Builds on: clause structure and prepared speech. Leads to: reading evidence and formal speeches.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: The room is open; the notice is ready. Bih’s notebook contains the draft. She wrote, “Bring a pen, a notebook and a folder.” The semicolon joins related complete clauses; the apostrophe identifies the owner; the quoted instruction has a readable list.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Find boundaries and ownership first. Apply the requested convention, reread for meaning and check paired quotation marks. Do not put a comma between an ordinary subject and its verb.

pick.q: Join these independent clauses using a semicolon: The room is open. The notice is ready.
pick.r: The room is open; the notice is ready.
w: The room is open, the notice is ready.
The room; is open the notice is ready.
The room is open the notice is ready.
e: A comma alone creates the comma splice being repaired.
That breaks the subject from its verb.
The clauses lack a boundary.
pick.y: A semicolon connects the related complete clauses.

pick.q: Use singular possession: the notebook belonging to Bih.
e: The possessive marker is missing.
That placement does not mark the named singular owner.
The marker belongs on the owner.

w: Bih, said The room is ready.
Bih said, The room is ready.
e: The closing quotation mark is missing.
This splits subject and verb and omits quotation marks.
The requested direct quotation needs speech marks.

pick.r: Bring a pen, a notebook and a folder.
w: Bring a pen a notebook and a folder.
Bring, a pen a notebook and a folder.
Bring a, pen a, notebook and a folder.
e: Separate the first list item.
The comma splits verb and object rather than items.
These commas split determiners from nouns.
pick.y: Separate items, not their internal noun groups.
